clue.text: So, a chosen few can be forced to make an appearance

indicators.note: something forced is pushed out of its natural shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A select few can be pressured into turning up at an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' is the anagram signal: the letters of SO A CHOSEN FEW are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To show one's face is an idiom for putting in an appearance, briefly turning up somewhere.

clue.text: Celebrity adopting Frenchwoman's speech impediment

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the celebrity word takes the other piece into itself

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
Mme, short for Madame, is the French title for a married woman

explanation.surface: A famous person takes on a Frenchwoman's way of speaking, perhaps for a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' is the containment signal: the celebrity takes in the French title rather than a French child.
explanation.definitionFit: A stammer is a speech disorder marked by involuntary repetition and blocking of sounds.

clue.text: Knock down walls of Durham steel town, for a start

indicators.note: demolishing the walls removes the outer edges, so the town's first and last letters go

parts.note: Consett, in County Durham, was a famous steel-making town

explanation.surface: A call to demolish part of a northern industrial town as a first step.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSETT is a former steelworks town in County Durham, England; 'Knock down walls of' removes its C and final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, especially something unwelcome like an illness.

clue.text: Give too much consideration to visible tattoo featuring husband

indicators.note: a design featuring something includes it within, so the husband letter sits inside the joined pieces

parts.note: overt means open and visible
ink is slang for a tattoo

explanation.surface: A conspicuous tattoo with a husband's name in it might cause someone to ponder too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' works as containment: the husband's initial appears within the tattooed design, as names often do.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthink something is to dwell on it excessively, analysing beyond what is useful.

clue.text: Dash from cycling path

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path or track

explanation.surface: Someone darts out of a bike lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final E of LANE round to the front. 'Dash' is the noun (verve), not a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and élan both mean stylish vigour or flair.

clue.text: Outrageous fat Elvis celebration

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wildly out of order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tribute event celebrating Elvis in his later, heavier years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outrageous' signals rearranging FAT ELVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a day or period of celebration, often a public event.

clue.text: Clever Johnny!

definitions.meaning: a john is slang for a toilet, as is a can, so a playful Johnny becomes CAN plus NY

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke: JOHN + NY with JOHN swapped for its slang twin CAN (both mean toilet).
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd and astute, especially in judging money or people.

clue.text: Adult working in dirty church steeples?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

indicators.note: in places the working word inside the dirty word

parts.note: grimy means dirty
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A grown-up labouring inside grubby church towers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal. The question mark flags that 'church steeples' is a folk name for a plant, not architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony, a yellow-flowered herb, has the folk name church steeples from its tall spikes.

clue.text: Research into the work of Picasso, say, is to stop

indicators.note: into puts the research piece within the art piece

parts.note: Picasso's paintings are an example of art
RES is a standard abbreviation for research

explanation.surface: A scholar's study of Picasso's paintings is to be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals containment; 'the work of Picasso, say' is a definition by example, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt it, as in arresting decline.

clue.text: Was easily converted, creating divisions in church

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone readily switched faith, causing a split in the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' signals rearranging WAS EASILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Aisleways are passages that separate the rows of pews in a church.

clue.text: Country in which Queen nearly overthrown

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, so the word is read backwards
nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, used in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A nation where a monarch was almost toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims REGINA to REGIN; 'overthrown' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Change lover, to inspire lust, from time to time

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the lover word takes in the other letters

parts.note: a mate is a partner or lover

indicators.note: from time to time means only now and then, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: Swapping partners to keep passion alive now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes the even letters of lust; 'to inspire', literally to breathe in, signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to undergo change, especially in form or genetic structure.

clue.text: According to Spooner, scientific adviser expressed disappointment throughout London?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the starting sounds of words, which is what happens here

parts.note: Chris Whitty, the UK's chief medical officer, was government chief scientific adviser
to sigh is to breathe out in disappointment

explanation.surface: A senior government scientist let out a weary breath.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITTY SIGHED with its opening sounds swapped becomes CITY WIDE. The question mark marks London as one example of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Citywide means extending across a whole city, and London is one such city.

clue.text: Terrible batter runs slightly around back of hob

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: around puts the slightly phrase around the last letter of the hob

parts.note: a bit means slightly

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A hopeless cricketer scrapes a few runs off the last of the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket slang a rabbit is a hopeless batsman. 'around' puts B, from 'back of' hob, inside A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is cricket slang for a player who cannot bat, usually a tail-ender.

clue.text: American wearing corset meets a British folk hero

indicators.note: the American is dressed in the corset, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a bodice is a close-fitting corset-like garment

explanation.surface: An American in a corset encounters a famous British figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' signals containment: the American is dressed in the corset. Boadicea, or Boudica, led a revolt against Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Boadicea was the Iceni queen who rose against the Romans, a celebrated British heroine.

clue.text: Order to retire, or continue with job?

parts.note: to last is to continue or endure
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Is this a signal to step down, or to stay on at work?
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is a military bugle call once sounded at day's end, sending troops to bed; 'retire' means go to bed, not stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post was the bugle call at day's end telling soldiers to go to their quarters.

clue.text: Prize toad has broken bone

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An award-winning toad has suffered a fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PRIZE TOAD; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapezoid is one of the eight small carpal bones of the wrist.

clue.text: Nobody stop Ian describing the worst of all worlds

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the outer words enclose the answer

explanation.surface: No one should stop Ian from portraying a terrible world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' signals the answer sits in nobODY STOP IAn.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society where everything is as bad as it could be, the opposite of utopia.

clue.text: Vital to stop British doctor creating visible injury

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the vital word fills the middle of the doctor word

parts.note: to doctor a drink is to lace it
key means vital or essential

explanation.surface: It is crucial to halt a British medic who is harming patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, to spike a drink, not a physician. 'to stop' means to plug, so the vital word fills a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A black eye is bruising around the eye, an injury plain for all to see.

clue.text: Prevent plot being designed to wound

parts.note: to bar is to prevent
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: Stopping a scheme intended to cause harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a patch of garden, a flower bed, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbed remarks are pointed and meant to hurt, like hooked barbs.

clue.text: Timber expert was backing you

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word was is read in reverse

parts.note: yer is a dialect form of you

explanation.surface: A woodworker supported you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses WAS to SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawyer is someone who saws timber for a living.

clue.text: End up overwhelmed by desire for uneducated labourer

indicators.note: a thing overwhelmed by another is engulfed in it, so it goes inside

parts.note: reck is an old verb meaning to care for or want

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone finishes consumed by longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the end word round in this down entry; 'overwhelmed by' signals containment in an archaic verb for caring about or wanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck is a derogatory US term for a poor, rural white manual worker, from sunburnt necks.

clue.text: Sit on the throne with it close to backside, and burn again

parts.note: to reign is to rule as monarch

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Settling on the toilet, with a sore rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit on the throne' looks like toilet humour but means to rule; 'close to' gives the E of backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reignite is to light or kindle once more.

clue.text: In-laws call regularly about Hooters

definitions.note: hooters is slang for noses, and nasal means relating to the nose

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: The in-laws phone now and again about a restaurant chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of IN-LAWS CALL. Hooters is slang for noses, not the restaurant chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, and hooter is British slang for the nose.

clue.text: Prancer video shows this?

indicators.note: shows means puts on display, so the answer is visible within the words

explanation.surface: A film of Santa's reindeer Prancer features this animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' exposes the answer in pranCER VIDeo, and Prancer is a deer, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cervid is a member of the deer family, Cervidae, to which reindeer like Prancer belong.

clue.text: Oscar enters into prostitution, say

indicators.note: enters into puts the Oscar letter inside the other word

parts.note: vice is a term for prostitution, as in a police vice squad
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An awards winner gets involved in the sex trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters into' puts O inside VICE after V.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to say it, and to have a voice is to have a say.

clue.text: About to support popular South American

indicators.note: in a down entry, the support goes underneath, so the about piece comes after the popular one

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Getting ready to back a well-liked man from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts CA below IN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the people of the Andean empire centred on Peru.

clue.text: Compares final five members of football and netball teams

indicators.note: only the last five letters are kept, dropping the opening pair

parts.note: football teams are elevens and netball teams are sevens; both end in the same five letters

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up the last five players in two kinds of sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENS works equally: either word's last five letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To even things is to make them equal or level, a loose synonym of comparing them.

clue.text: Intend to quietly act bit of Loot out in show

indicators.note: out means removed, so this letter is taken away

parts.note: to plan to is to intend to

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

parts.note: to mime is to act without words

explanation.surface: Planning to perform a silent scene from Joe Orton's play Loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes L from Loot, and 'out' removes it from PLAN TO. A pantomime is a British Christmas stage comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a theatrical entertainment, a type of stage show.

clue.text: It requires strength, being honourable with idiot

parts.note: clean means honourable or above board
and means with or together with
a jerk is a fool

explanation.surface: Being decent alongside a fool takes inner strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The clean and jerk is a weightlifting move lifting the bar to the shoulders and then overhead.
